sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax
sections.html:
Three layers of government share the bill. The county, one of 14 school districts and, in most places, one of the 73 municipalities each levy a tax. The County Assessment Office puts a value on every parcel those levies are applied to. Delinquent bills are the job of the Tax Claim Bureau, which answers to the county commissioners.

State-certified assessors set the values. Whenever an assessment is created or changed, the owner is mailed a Change in Assessment notice, and school districts and municipalities get the same data so they can bill the new amount. The Assessment Office is at 313 W. Market St., Suite 4202, West Chester, phone 610-344-6105, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

sections.h2: How a tax bill is calculated
sections.html:
The formula is assessment times millage. A mill is one-thousandth of assessed value, so a rate of 5.164 mills equals 0.005164.

In Chester County the assessment equals 100% of appraised market value as of the base year. The last countywide reassessment took effect for 1998, and the Common Level Ratio exists to account for the gap between assessments and current sale prices. When the Assessment Office prices new work, it uses the computer-assisted mass appraisal model built before that reassessment, and it can't apply the Common Level Ratio to its own figures. Elected officials vote millage rates by dividing the budget by the tax base, so county, school and municipal rates differ by address. Ask the Assessment Office or your municipality for the rates on your parcel.

An annual appeal runs from May 1 through the first business day in August, and the same window covers exemption appeals. A Board decision on an annual appeal doesn't change your bill until the following tax year.

Chester County assessment appeal windows and fees
Appeal typeFiling windowFee
Annual, residentialMay 1 to first business day in August$25
Annual, Clean and Green or Act 515 parcelMay 1 to first business day in August$50
Annual, commercial or industrial, and exemptionsMay 1 to first business day in August$150
Interim, after new construction40 days from the Change in Assessment noticeSame fee by property type

Print the form, complete it and return it to the office, since faxes and electronic copies are refused. The fee isn't refunded if you skip the hearing or withdraw. Owners over 60 who can't pay the $25 can call the Department of Aging at 610-344-6350 about help.

A three-member Board of Assessment Appeals, appointed by the county commissioners for four-year terms, hears each case. Notices go out at least 20 days ahead, and hearings are held at the Government Services Center, 601 Westtown Rd., West Goshen Township.

  • Bring recent photographs of the front and rear of the house, taken within the last six months.
  • Bring appraisals or sale records for similar homes nearby.
  • If you can't attend, send someone with a letter of authorization. Only one of several joint owners needs to appear.

The Board decides a fair market value and then applies the Common Level Ratio, set at 30.6% for annual appeals heard in 2026, with decisions effective for tax bills issued in 2027. Written decisions normally arrive within three to four weeks, though annual appeal results aren't mailed until after August 1. If you disagree, you can go to the Court of Common Pleas within 30 days of the Board's notice.

sections.h2: Homestead exclusion and Clean and Green
sections.html:
The Homestead and Farmstead Exclusion lowers the assessed value of an owner-occupied home, though not a rental or business-only property. Enrollment runs December 15 through the first business day in March, with no fee. Approval isn't automatic. The exclusion shows as a line on the bill, and an approved owner can't be made to reapply more than once every three years. If you move, apply again for the new home.

The Clean and Green program under Act 319 takes applications from March 1 through June 1, filed with the Assessment Office. If you improve a house, know about interim assessments too: a new addition, pool, garage or shed raises the assessment from the first month after completion, and the taxing authorities then bill the increase.

sections.h2: What happens when taxes go unpaid
sections.html:
Taxes are due by December 31 of the year they're levied, and whatever is unpaid after that is delinquent. Taxing authorities certify unpaid liens to the Tax Claim Bureau by January 15, and return and claim notices go out by certified mail by July 31. The bureau works under the Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act 542 of 1947.

  • An upset sale is scheduled no earlier than the second Monday in September and no later than September 30 of year two.
  • The sale is advertised at least 30 days ahead, and a second notice goes by first class mail at least 10 days before.
  • The bid price covers current and delinquent taxes, municipal and Commonwealth liens, transfer taxes, recording fees and costs.
  • The court must confirm the sale absolute, a step that takes about four to six months before funds are paid out.
  • An unsold property becomes eligible for a judicial sale, which sells it free and clear of liens and mortgages.

Owners can head off a sale with an agreement requiring at least 25% down and three equal installments, or a deferral of up to twelve months. The bureau grants both at its discretion.

Chester County has about 557,116 residents in 751 square miles around West Chester, and Coatesville is the only city. The median owner-occupied value is $485,600 for 2020 to 2024, median household income is $127,208 and owner-occupancy is 75.1%. At those values, even a small gap between assessed and market value can make an appeal worthwhile.

If you carry unpaid tax, call both the Tax Claim Bureau and the Assessment Office. Ask each for the current balance and any interim assessment pending on the parcel before you agree to a closing date. Municipal permit offices hand owners a county letter explaining that improvements are assessed, and a certified Pennsylvania evaluator visits to collect property data. A buyer's lender will want the billing history clean, so settle any pending interim notice early.

Pull your latest bills and your Change in Assessment notices. Check whether the homestead exclusion is on the bill. If an annual appeal window is open, gather photographs and comparable sales. Call the Assessment Office at 610-344-6105 about any pending interim assessment, and the Tax Claim Bureau about any balance. Then give your closing agent the figures in writing so nothing surfaces on settlement day.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Chester County property assessment?
faqs.a: Annual appeals may be filed from May 1 through the first business day in August. Interim appeals after new construction must be filed within 40 days of the Change in Assessment notice.

faqs.q: How much does a Chester County assessment appeal cost?
faqs.a: A residential appeal costs $25, a Clean and Green or Act 515 parcel costs $50, and commercial, industrial and exemption appeals cost $150. The fee is paid at filing and isn't refunded.

faqs.q: When does Chester County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: Taxes become delinquent after December 31 of the year they are levied. Unpaid taxes can lead to an upset sale held between the second Monday of September and September 30 of the following year.

faqs.q: Can I stop a Chester County tax sale?
faqs.a: Possibly. The Tax Claim Bureau can offer an agreement with 25% down and three equal installments, or a deferral of up to twelve months. Both options are discretionary, so call the bureau before the sale.

faqs.q: How do I apply for the homestead exclusion in Chester County?
faqs.a: Apply to the Assessment-Homestead Office between December 15 and the first business day in March. There is no filing fee, and approval isn't automatic for owner-occupied homes.
